title: Finished tool jobs piled up in Redis until it was killed for memory
problem: The tool job stream kept every finished job. It reached 219 MB and Redis was killed for memory over and over, taking live values and locks with it.
fix: A job is deleted once it is acknowledged, old finished jobs are cleared on start, and the stream has a size cap.

title: Redis could be killed for memory instead of refusing writes
problem: Local Redis had no maxmemory, so a runaway key grew until the container was killed, and production evicted keys silently, queues and locks included.
fix: Redis runs with a maxmemory below its limit and noeviction, so writes fail loudly, and a RedisMemoryHigh alert fires above 85%.

title: Scaling the agent runtime down killed runs that were still going
problem: KEDA removed a runtime pod in the middle of an agent's run. The run was left showing running with nothing working on it.
fix: A pod that is told to stop finishes the runs it holds first, pools scale down one pod at a time, and a run whose pod is gone fails with WORKER_STOPPED and a plain message.

title: An unexpected server error showed as Failed to fetch
problem: A 500 went out without CORS headers, so the browser hid it and every server error looked like the network was down.
fix: Unexpected errors answer 500 in the usual envelope with CORS headers and a reference id.

title: Two agents could share a slug and creating an agent then failed
problem: Saving an agent reset its slug from its name even when the name was unchanged, so two agents ended up with the same slug and agent creation failed.
fix: The slug only moves when the name really changes and only to a free slug. A unique index enforces it and existing duplicates were renamed.

title: An approval notified everyone in the workspace
problem: Every approval sent a notice to every user, one by one before answering, so asking took seconds and people who could not decide were told.
fix: Only the people who can decide are told, and the notices go out in the background.

title: Dialogs opened half off the screen and lost typed text on resize
problem: A dialog started in its phone layout, so on desktop it sat half below the screen, and resizing across tablet width lost what was typed.
fix: A dialog decides its layout when it opens and keeps it until it closes.

title: A Sparkplug device kept signals its new birth no longer declared
problem: Signals left over from an earlier birth stayed in the live view for ever.
fix: A birth replaces the device's signal set. Undeclared signals are marked retired and their history stays.

title: Devices without births never went offline
problem: Devices on Kafka, RabbitMQ, HTTP push and other sources stayed online for hours after they went quiet, so counts, banners, forget and stale rules were wrong.
fix: A device goes offline after a silence learnt from its own pace, from 60 seconds to 15 minutes, and its offline time is when it really went quiet.

title: Shared Kafka and HTTP push devices flapped offline
problem: A replica that stopped hearing a device marked it offline while another replica was still receiving it.
fix: A replica checks the shared record before marking a device offline, and a wrong flag heals within 2 seconds.

title: A workspace over its device limit had no way out
problem: Hitting the device limit blocked new devices and the UI offered nothing but the banner.
fix: Devices can be forgotten one at a time or in bulk with a dry run, the banner offers it in one click, and devices offline for 30 days are forgotten on their own.

title: Testbed signals had physical units the simulator did not produce
problem: The OPC UA testbed mapped one rising counter to temperature, pressure and vibration, so all three showed the same value with units.
fix: Signals are named for what the simulator produces, only the simulated boiler temperature carries a unit, and a test refuses any other.
